correctness.rationale: For x∈A,y∈B the internal-pair potential W=within(A)/a+within(B)/b has ΔW equal to the sum of both agents’ cost reductions; therefore any strictly mutually improving swap increases W and terminates after at most binom(n,a)−1 swaps. A sorted-type gap decomposition gives contribution k−j²/a−(k−j)²/b at prefix k, individually maximized by j_k=floor(ak/n+1/2). The rounded sequence is a feasible 0–1 increment path and global W maximizer (equilibrium). Social cross cost is minimized by maximizing unweighted within-pair sum, whose prefix optimizer is j_k=clamp_{[max(0,k−b),min(a,k)]}(floor((a−b+2k)/4+1/2)), also a feasible path. Exact K2,5 seven-agent witness [0,0,0,0,1,3,4] has minimum cross cost 15 but minimum equilibrium cross cost 17, PoS17/15; independent brute all 21 pair allocations reproduced both and 9 labeled equilibria. Median star center minimizes cost and is equilibrium; triangle inequality gives sharp PoA≤n−1 for nonconstant profiles.
